am.nc.0001.gold_step: Either update the database so both axes belong to the same logical machine, or transfer one axis at run time so both share a logical machine before enabling the cam.
am.nc.0001.support: An axis can be transferred between between logical machines using the following commands.

am.nc.0001.gold_step: Re-enable the electronic cam once both axes are on the same logical machine.
am.nc.0001.support: Just as with a mechanical cam, the electronic cam function on the CNC allows the coupling of two axes.

am.nc.0002.gold_step: Coordinate the transfer using DETACH, BARRIER and ATTACH in the correct order.
am.nc.0002.support: The first barrier ensures that PPP1 has detached the `A` axis from LM1, before PPP2 attempts to attach that axis to LM2.

am.nc.0002.gold_step: Use a BARRIER to synchronise the logical machines so the axis is free at the point of ATTACH.
am.nc.0002.support: | [`attach`](./05-functions.md#attach)   | function | Attaches an axis to the current logical machine.          |

am.nc.0003.gold_step: Decide whether M101 should be implemented in PLC or as an EPPL part program.
am.nc.0003.support: Other M-codes (modes 1-3 and 5-7) are instead implemented via the PLC and do not trigger part programs.

am.nc.0004.gold_step: Distinguish control points from the start/end points.
am.nc.0004.support: Start, end and dummy points: the start point of a spline is the end point of the previous move, and the end point is the last control point before `splineoff`.

am.nc.0005.gold_step: Split them across separate blocks so each block has at most one class 1 word.
am.nc.0005.support: This section concentrates on the three methods of categorising preparatory words; classes, modes and groups; and the rules which govern the programming of several preparatory words in the same block.
Commands and words that may be legally included within a single block are executed independently of the order in which they were programmed.

am.cfg.0001.gold_step: Reconfigure one of them to use a different device address.
am.cfg.0001.support: Determine the logical address of the device (it was set when you [set up your devices](./set-up-your-devices/set-up-your-devices.md#set-up-your-devices)).

am.cfg.0001.gold_step: Restart AMCore and confirm startup completes without the assertion.

am.lic.0001.gold_step: If you do need it, contact ANCA to add the OPC UA option to your license.
am.lic.0001.support:

**Type:** `String` | `CN=ANCA Motion AMCore`
`OPC UA Server` | Subject field of certificate.

This value must match the subject field of the certificate. |

am.fb.0001.gold_step: Note the device name and station address in the message.
am.fb.0001.support: | Name | Description | | Current state | Actual operational state of the device |

am.fb.0001.gold_step: If the same device drops out again, restart (power-cycle) that drive specifically.
am.fb.0001.support: A device will raise a device unexpected state error when its operational state no longer matches that of the Master.

am.fb.0002.gold_step: An emergency with error code zero is informational (the drive recovered) — just acknowledge it.
am.fb.0002.support: Note that emergencies with an error code set to zero is an informational message that some drives raise when it has successfully recovered from an emergency.

am.fb.0003.gold_step: Check the error type (No Response, CRC, Retry Fail, etc.) for the nature of the fault.
am.fb.0003.support: | Error type | Type of frame response error |

am.fb.0003.gold_step: Single spurious errors often self-recover — no action needed.
am.fb.0003.support: Sometimes these errors are spurious, and the drive is able to recover itself.

am.fb.0003.gold_step: If they repeat, they usually escalate to a drive emergency; a system restart is then required.
am.fb.0003.support: Sometimes these errors are spurious, and the drive is able to recover itself.

am.fb.0003.gold_step: For detail, review the logs at %amcore%/PCC/dsa.log and %amcore%/PCC/ecatmaster.log.

am.fb.0004.gold_step: Start AMCore with 'AMCore.exe -start device' to bring the fieldbus to PREOP via the Device Administrator.
am.fb.0004.support: (docs/docs-proto/starter-kit/docs/user-guide/use-amcore/device-firmware-upgrade.md) Firmware uploads require the EtherCAT fieldbus to be in a non-operational state (INIT or PREOP).

am.fb.0004.gold_step: Upload the firmware (interactive device-firmware-upload tool, automatic mode, or the CNCC SDK / FoE).
am.fb.0004.support: (docs/docs-proto/starter-kit/docs/user-guide/use-amcore/device-firmware-upgrade.md) Firmware uploads use the FoE (File over EtherCAT) mailbox protocol.

am.fb.0004.gold_step: On success run 'AMCore.exe -start' to continue to OP; on failure run 'AMCore.exe -stop'.
am.fb.0004.support: > If you call `AMCore.exe -start` without first calling `AMCore.exe -start device`, the system proceeds directly to OP and firmware uploads will be rejected with `CNCCRESULT_INVALID_FIELDBUS_STATE`.
